## Key terms

{{< glossary digital-skills digital-literacy digital-competence digcomp competence-area proficiency-level labour-market lifelong-learning >}}

## 1.1 Skills, literacy and competence

**Digital skills** are practical abilities with devices and applications.
**Digital literacy** adds judgement: finding, evaluating, creating and
communicating information critically and safely. **Digital competence** is the
widest: knowledge, skills and attitudes for confident, critical and
responsible use. Skills are described at three levels: **basic** (everyday
tasks), **intermediate** (productive use at work) and **advanced** (creating
and managing technology — ICT specialists).

![Skills ⊂ literacy ⊂ competence.](images/skills-circles.png){width=62%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Which term, which level?"}
Choose the right term or level.

::: {.match}
The practical ability to use devices and applications.
:   digital skills

Finding, evaluating and communicating information critically and safely.
:   digital literacy

Knowledge, skills and attitudes for confident, responsible use.
:   digital competence

Filling in an online form.
:   basic level

Analysing sales data in a spreadsheet at work.
:   intermediate level

Programming a game or administering servers.
:   advanced level
:::
:::

## 1.2 The DigComp framework

**DigComp 2.2** (European Commission, 2022) describes digital competence in
**5 areas** and **21 competences**: information and data literacy;
communication and collaboration; digital content creation; safety; problem
solving. Each competence has **8 proficiency levels** in four bands —
foundation (1–2), intermediate (3–4), advanced (5–6), highly specialised
(7–8) — that grow in complexity, autonomy and cognitive level. Programming is
only one of the 21 competences.

![The five areas and 21 competences of DigComp 2.2.](images/digcomp-areas.png){width=96%}

![The eight proficiency levels in four bands.](images/proficiency.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Place it in DigComp"}
Choose the competence, the number or the band.

::: {.match extra="2.6 managing digital identity"}
Checking whether a forum post is a reliable source.
:   1.2 evaluating data and content

Writing polite, clear messages in the team chat.
:   2.5 netiquette

Checking the licence of a free sound effect.
:   3.3 copyright and licences

Installing the security updates of a phone.
:   4.1 protecting devices

Noticing a missing skill and taking a course.
:   5.4 identifying competence gaps

The number of competences in DigComp 2.2.
:   21

The band of levels 5–6.
:   advanced
:::
:::

## 1.3 Digital skills and the labour market

Work is digitalised; **automation** takes over routine tasks and raises the
demand for people who use and check digital tools; governments set targets —
the EU Digital Decade aims for **80 %** of adults with basic digital skills
and **20 million** ICT specialists by 2030. Because tools change, employers
value **lifelong learning**. In a game studio every role — tester, designer,
producer, marketer — relies on its own mix of DigComp areas.

![EU targets for 2030.](images/eu-targets.png){width=76%}

![Every role in a studio depends on digital tools.](images/studio.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Skills at work"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="50 %|programming"}
The EU target for adults with at least basic digital skills by 2030.
:   80 %

The EU target for employed ICT specialists by 2030.
:   20 million

Learning new tools throughout one's working life.
:   lifelong learning

The kind of tasks that automation takes over first.
:   routine tasks

A community manager's weekly engagement report in a spreadsheet: the DigComp area.
:   information and data literacy
:::
:::

## Game challenge: hiring at Pixel Harbor {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Pixel Harbor** is a mobile-game studio of eight people, partly working from
home. It is hiring a junior QA tester and a junior marketing assistant. The
tester will write bug reports in a shared tracker; the marketing assistant
will create short videos for social media. Every employee must use two-factor
authentication. Candidates describe their skills with DigComp areas and levels.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Read the candidates (harder)"}
Choose the DigComp area or the proficiency band.

::: {.match extra="problem solving|highly specialised"}
Bug reports in a shared tracker.
:   communication and collaboration

Short videos for social media.
:   digital content creation

Two-factor authentication for every employee.
:   safety

A candidate who can share a file only with help.
:   foundation

A candidate who trains colleagues in a new tool.
:   advanced
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Skills (abilities) ⊂ literacy (judgement) ⊂ competence (knowledge, skills, attitudes).
- Levels: basic, intermediate, advanced (ICT specialists).
- DigComp 2.2: 5 areas, 21 competences, 8 levels in 4 bands.
- Programming is one competence of 21.
- Digitalisation, automation and policy put digital skills at the centre of the labour market.
- Lifelong learning starts with finding your own gaps.
